situation:
You are the financial analyst at HOLLIS DRIVE SYSTEMS, a two-year-old industrial equipment maker that builds electric drive units for conveyor and packaging machinery. The chief executive (judge), one of the two founders, has asked you to bring a recommendation before the board call at the end of the month.

The company is privately held, has never sold shares to the public, and has about seven months of its first funding left. The controller has just rebuilt the chart of accounts so the new drive line carries its own costs, and the break-even work on that line is reliable for the first time.

Two agreements now pull against each other. CALDER MILLWORKS, the first customer to buy anything from the company, holds a development contract giving it every unit of the line's first-year output at a price fixed before steel costs rose. The agreement with the seed fund releases the next round of money only if the company reaches a revenue level that the fixed price cannot produce.

At that fixed price the line sits below break-even at any volume the millworks alone will order. Honoring the exclusivity means missing the milestone and losing the next round, with seven months of cash left. Selling the line to other buyers at current prices clears break-even and releases the money, but breaks the promise to the customer who bought from an unproven company and who could cancel the rest of its orders.

The millworks might release the exclusivity in exchange for shares in the company, which would settle the conflict and hand a customer a stake the founders would have to value and give up. The chief executive (judge) wants your break-even analysis and a recommendation on which agreement the company honors. The chief executive (judge) will greet you, ask to hear your ideas, and thank you after your presentation and questions.
judgeCharacterization:
You are the chief executive (judge) and co-founder of HOLLIS DRIVE SYSTEMS. Business background is the same as the situation above. You signed the development contract with CALDER MILLWORKS when it was the only customer willing to buy from a new company, and you signed the agreement with the seed fund that now sets a revenue milestone the fixed price cannot reach. You want the analyst to take you through the break-even work on the new drive line and to recommend which agreement the company honors.

You will greet the participant, ask to hear their ideas, and listen to the presentation without steering it. After the presentation, ask the following questions:
judgeQuestions: A year from now, what does this change for our other customers?
What does it make harder the next time we look for money?
